body:
### Summary of Sync Logic Changes

Previously, the app's sync function would fetch all data from the server and completely overwrite the local database. We've replaced this with a more intelligent **incremental merge** strategy.

Now, when a sync is initiated:

1.  **Incoming data is compared to local data.** The app fetches the latest records from the server and compares them against the records already stored on the device, using the `resource_id` to match them.

2.  **Updates are based on a timestamp.** An `updated_at` timestamp is used to determine if a change is needed. An existing record is only updated if the incoming version is newer. This prevents unnecessary database writes and improves performance.

3.  **A single "upsert" operation handles changes.** We use the existing `cacheFhirResources` function to efficiently handle both **creating** new records (if the ID doesn't exist locally) and **updating** existing ones (if the incoming record is newer).

In short, the sync logic no longer blindly replaces data. It now performs a smart, row-by-row merge that preserves your local database, adds new records, updates only what has changed, ensuring data is always consistent and up-to-date without unnecessary data loss.

body:
This PR introduces a new **document scanning workflow,** allowing users to digitize physical medical documents and attach them to encounters.

It also includes an experimental feature to parse these documents using a local language model (Gemma 2B) to automatically generate medical records.

### Key changes

#### 1. Document Capture & Import:
- Integrates a new scanning interface for capturing documents with the device camera.

- Adds functionality for users to import existing photos from their device gallery.

- Allows users to select and import documents (e.g., PDFs) from their device files.

- All imported/scanned documents can be successfully attached to an existing encounter.

#### 2. AI-Assisted Record Generation
- Adds a new workflow to process the content of the aforementioned documents.

- This process uses a local, 4-bit quantized gemma-2b-it model.

- Based on specific prompts, the model generates draft medical records populated with extracted information (e.g., patient data, vitals, notes). The user can then review these records and make changes to them before they are saved.

#### 3. Changes to database structure
- These changes are done in order to accommodate modifications to records done in the app
- Makes external sources (i.e. coming from Fasten, or other EHRs) read-only to prevent data inconsistency.
- Changes how the relation between the patient and source entity is handled.
- Introduces the concept of "wallet" sources which are, going forward, the places where records that are modified or added through the app are kept.

title: Fix on Android device to not crash the app
body:
## Add Printing Support - Fix Android Crash (HM-121)

### Problem
The app was crashing on Android due to the `pdf_to_image_converter` package (https://pub.dev/packages/pdf_to_image_converter) and its dependencies. This package relied on `image_gallery_saver` and `pdf_image_renderer`, which were causing compatibility issues and app crashes on Android.

### Solution
Replaced the problematic `pdf_to_image_converter` package with the stable `printing` package (v5.14.2) which provides better PDF handling and printing capabilities across all platforms.

### Changes
- **Removed problematic dependencies:**
  - `pdf_to_image_converter` (was causing Android crashes)
  - `image_gallery_saver` (dependency of pdf_to_image_converter)
  - `pdf_image_renderer` (dependency of pdf_to_image_converter)

- **Added new dependency:**
  - `printing ^5.14.2` - Stable, well-maintained package for PDF printing functionality

- **Localization updates:**
  - Added missing translations for `walletHolder` and `walletHolderDescription` in German and Spanish

- **Platform updates:**
  - Updated generated plugin registrants for iOS, Android, Linux, macOS, and Windows

### Technical Details
- Updated `pubspec.lock` and `ios/Podfile.lock` with dependency changes
- Generated plugin registrants updated for cross-platform support
- Minor dependency version adjustments (e.g., SDWebImage 5.21.3 → 5.21.2)

### Testing
- ✅ Verify PDF printing functionality works correctly
- ✅ Confirm Android crash is resolved
- ✅ Test on all supported platforms (iOS, Android, Linux, macOS, Windows)

## Summary
Implement automated deployment workflows with branch-specific strategies for efficient CI/CD pipeline.

## Workflow Configuration

### 📱 **Develop Branch** (Fast Iteration)
- **PR Creation**: No workflows run
- **PR Merge**: Auto-deploy iOS & Android directly
  - iOS → TestFlight (beta)
  - Android → Play Store Internal Track
- **Goal**: Fast deployment for testing

### 🏆 **Master Branch** (Production Quality)
- **PR Creation**: CI runs (analyze & test)
- **PR Merge**: Auto-deploy iOS & Android
  - iOS → TestFlight (beta)
  - Android → Play Store Internal Track
- **Goal**: Code validated before deployment, no redundant CI

## Changes

### New Files
- `.github/workflows/master-deploy.yml` - Deploy workflow for master branch

### Modified Files
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` - Only runs on PRs to master
- `.github/workflows/ios-deploy.yml` - Auto-triggers on develop push
- `.github/workflows/android-deploy.yml` - Auto-triggers on develop push
- `pubspec.yaml` - Version bump to 1.2.0+10

## Build Number Handling
- Build numbers auto-increment from App Store Connect & Play Store APIs
- iOS fetches latest TestFlight build and increments
- Android fetches latest Play Store build and increments
- pubspec.yaml build number is ignored during deployment

Manual workflow_dispatch still available for custom deployments:
```bash
gh workflow run ios-deploy.yml --ref <branch> -f lane=beta|release
gh workflow run android-deploy.yml --ref <branch> -f track=internal|production
```

title: refactor: Unified Deploy Workflow Structure
body:
## Summary
Create clean, consistent deployment workflow structure with unified deploy workflows for each branch.

## New Structure

### 🚀 **Deploy Workflows**

**1. Develop Deploy** (`develop-deploy.yml`)
- **Trigger**: Push to `develop`
- **Jobs**: Deploy iOS & Android in parallel
- **No CI**: Fast iteration workflow

**2. Master Deploy** (`master-deploy.yml`)
- **Trigger**: Push to `master`
- **Jobs**: Deploy iOS & Android in parallel
- **No CI in workflow**: CI already ran during PR validation

### ✅ **CI Workflow**

**3. CI** (`ci.yml`)
- **Trigger**: PRs to `master` only
- **Jobs**: Analyze & Test
- **Purpose**: Validate code before merge

### 🔧 **Manual Workflows**

**4. iOS Deploy (Manual)** (`ios-deploy.yml`)
- **Trigger**: `workflow_dispatch` only
- **Options**: beta or release lane
- **Purpose**: Ad-hoc iOS deployments

**5. Android Deploy (Manual)** (`android-deploy.yml`)
- **Trigger**: `workflow_dispatch` only
- **Options**: internal or production track
- **Purpose**: Ad-hoc Android deployments

## Workflow Flow

```
┌─────────────────┐       ┌─────────────────┐
│  Develop Branch │       │  Master Branch  │
└────────┬────────┘       └────────┬────────┘
         │                         │
    Push/Merge              Create PR → CI runs
         │                         │
         ▼                    Merge PR
┌────────────────┐                 │
│ Develop Deploy │                 ▼
├────────────────┤       ┌─────────────────┐
│ • iOS Deploy   │       │  Master Deploy  │
│ • Android Deploy│      ├─────────────────┤
└────────────────┘       │ • iOS Deploy    │
                         │ • Android Deploy│
                         └─────────────────┘
```

## Changes

**New:**
- `.github/workflows/develop-deploy.yml` - Unified develop deployment

**Modified:**
- `.github/workflows/ios-deploy.yml` - Manual trigger only
- `.github/workflows/android-deploy.yml` - Manual trigger only

## Benefits

✅ Consistent structure between develop and master  
✅ Clear separation of automated vs manual workflows  
✅ No redundant CI runs  
✅ Parallel iOS & Android deployments  
✅ Easy to understand workflow organization

title: feat: v1.3.0 — desktop app, on-device AI, attachment browser, specialty cards
body:
## What's new in v1.3.0

### AI document processing on Mac
HealthWallet can now process your health documents entirely on your Mac — no internet connection required. When you import a scan or PDF, the on-device AI model (Qwen3-VL) reads the document, extracts structured health data, and maps it to FHIR records automatically. The Mac's hardware is used directly, bypassing the need to offload to a mobile device. You can also trigger processing from your iPhone and have your Mac do the heavy lifting via the Handover flow — useful when your phone doesn't have enough memory for inference.

### Sync with your iPhone via QR code
Pair your iPhone and Mac once by scanning a QR code shown on the desktop app. After pairing, the two devices stay in sync automatically over your local network — no iCloud, no third-party servers. Any health records you add, edit, or delete on one device propagate to the other using a Last-Write-Wins sync protocol with conflict resolution. The connection uses AES-256-GCM encryption over TCP, with MultipeerConnectivity as a fallback when a VPN or firewall blocks direct LAN access.

### New way to browse your health documents
The records browser now offers two modes: **Attachments view** shows your documents as a scrollable visual timeline with thumbnail previews, a year/month scrubber, and a full detail panel — ideal for quickly locating a specific scan or lab report by date. **Records list view** shows the structured FHIR data extracted from your documents, grouped by type. You can switch between modes freely and share records directly from either view.

### Organize by specialty
Your health dashboard now groups records by medical specialty — Cardiology, Oncology, Neurology, Orthopedics, and more. Each specialty card on the home screen shows a count of relevant records and lets you jump straight to a filtered view. Cards are fully reorderable so you can surface the specialties most relevant to you. The classifier runs locally against your existing records and updates automatically as new documents are processed.

---

## Test plan

- [ ] Import a PDF on Mac — AI processes it and creates FHIR records without internet
- [ ] Handover: trigger processing from iPhone, confirm Mac runs the pipeline and syncs results back
- [ ] Pair iPhone and Mac via QR code; edit a record on one device and confirm it appears on the other
- [ ] MPC fallback: connect while VPN is active and confirm sync still works
- [ ] Attachments view: timeline scrubber navigates by year/month; thumbnails render correctly
- [ ] Records list view: records grouped by type, share flow launches correctly from list
- [ ] Ephemeral viewer: thumbnails/timeline scrubber sit above `SessionBottomBar` on tablet
- [ ] Specialty cards appear on home dashboard; reordering persists across restarts
- [ ] Specialty classifier assigns correct specialty to Cardiology, Oncology, Neurology records
- [ ] System tray icon visible on macOS/Windows; minimize-to-tray and restore work
- [ ] Incoming Health Records dialog and `SelectionBottomBar` are constrained width on tablet
- [ ] l10n strings display correctly in DE/ES/RO

## Licence (HM-206)

- **Licensor:** Life Value (legal name: SC TECH STACK APPS SRL)
- **Free production use:** personal use by individuals, for their own health records and those of people in their care.
- **Commercial licence required:** every organization, including companies, providers, payers, networks, **government and public bodies**, schools and charities, and anyone offering the app or a modified version as a product or service.
- **Change Date:** each version converts to GPL-3.0 four years after it is published (BUSL requires a conversion within at most 4 years).
- Versions before 1.3.0, including all `v1.3.0-dev.*` pre-releases, **stay GPL-3.0**. That can't be revoked.

PolyForm Noncommercial was rejected because it explicitly makes government institutions free users.

`CONTRIBUTING.md` adds a Contributor License Agreement, accepted with `git commit -s`, so outside contributions can be licensed commercially.
